obligations.note: The change adds `if payee.category == "tax_authority": continue` in `purge_due`, which unconditionally prevents NPI purging for tax-authority payees regardless of the retention period. The obligation states that NPI of closed payee accounts must be purged after the approved retention period (84 months) and only be retained under legal hold. This new skip is a separate condition from the existing `legal_hold` check and has no equivalent in the obligation's exception clause.

The change introduces a deviation from RET-1 (tax-authority payees are never purged), but the exception register contains no approved, in-scope exception for RET-1 on the payments.retention component. The only registered exceptions cover SES-1 (expired), LOG-1 (mortgage), and MFA-1 (withdrawn), none of which apply.

Ticket CHG-25557 exists, is approved by change manager Erik Brandt, and its components list includes 'payments.retention', which is the component assigned to the changed file `retention.py` in `components.json`.

Sofia Santos (sofia.santos@fernbrook.example) holds the `change_approver` role for the payments app and is not the author (Jonah Weiss). Her code_review approval on the head commit satisfies the independent-approval requirement.
The approval names commit bfa403d, which is the sole and head commit of the change. There are no later commits that could void the approval.

The CI run (run.json) executed on the head commit bfa403d and reported success with 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. The registered control test for RET-1 (`test_sampled_purge_respects_hold`) ran and passed, along with all other control tests for obligations whose scope the change touches.

summary: The change adds a categorical skip in the retention purge job so that payees tagged 'tax_authority' are never purged, directly contradicting RET-1, which requires NPI of closed payee accounts to be purged after the approved retention period (only legal hold is an accepted exception). No exception in the register covers this deviation, so EXC-1 is also violated. While the change-management process obligations (CHG-1 through CHG-4) are satisfied—ticket approved, independent code review by a qualified non-author, approval covers the sole commit, and CI passed on the final commit—the substantive product-obligation violation is not curable by process compliance. The change must be rejected or an approved exception with a compensating control must be recorded before it can be reconsidered.
